prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create the FIRST COMIC PAGE in a two-page game-opening sequence. The existing garden journey comic in Image 1 is PAGE TWO. This new first page tells the origin and loss of home of the same thumb-sized wick spirit. One polished horizontal 16:9 watercolor comic image.

REFERENCE ROLES:
Image 1 = AUTHORITATIVE approved five-panel layout, parchment presentation, watercolor style and visual continuity for the immediately following page. Keep essentially its exact gently-slanted upper-two/lower-three arrangement, wide paper gutters and outer margins. Replace every illustrated scene with the new lamp-origin story described below; no greenhouse or garden environment on this first page.
Image 2 = exact character identity and body proportions.
Image 3 = character watercolor texture, creamy luminosity and mood reference.

PRESENTATION INVARIANTS:
Landscape 16:9. Exactly FIVE polygonal panels: two broad trapezoids across the upper row, then two narrower slanted panels at bottom-left and bottom-center and a wider last panel at bottom-right, matching Image 1. Retain its selected moderately slanted cuts and generous natural cream parchment gaps; do not change to a sharp lightning-bolt zigzag or a rectangular grid. Thin sepia outlines. Pale ivory aged storybook parchment with delicate fibers and very faint warm edge mottling. No scroll rolls, burned edges, titles, captions, speech balloons, panel numbers or text anywhere. All artwork stays within separate panel shapes.

STORY AND VISUAL SEQUENCE:
The protagonist is a thumb-sized wick spirit, a tiny living creature that normally inhabits sheltered crevices inside human lamps. It is good at REDIRECTING LIGHT THAT ALREADY EXISTS to where it is needed. It does not conjure light or use its own body as the power source for a whole room. A household once gave it a home in an old table lamp. The household moves away, the old lamp is dismantled and left broken, and the spirit becomes a wanderer. Begin warm, lived-in and sheltered; gradually become silent, empty and cool; finish at cloudy dusk ready for the stone-wall journey on page two.

CONTINUOUS LAMP DESIGN across all four indoor scenes:
One recognizable HUMAN-SIZED OLD TABLE LAMP: weathered slender brass stem with a simple curved neck, ivory opaque-glass bell/cone shade over a normal electric bulb, wide round warm-ivory ceramic base with a narrow dark seam/gap under its rim, subtle old patina. Ordinary tabletop scale, NOT a gigantic street lantern, oil lantern, candle, magical building or fairy house. The spirit is about 3 cm tall and the lamp about 45 cm tall; a tabletop pencil, broad wood grain and a book establish scale. A small opening/seam in the base is its protected hiding place. Do not depict a dollhouse door or miniature furniture built into the lamp.
The same lamp silhouette, ceramic color and brass stem recur through the panels. Lamp ON in panels 1–2; OFF, unplugged and dismantled after the household leaves in panels 3–4. A cracked/chipped shade or separated ceramic base in panel 4 makes the broken lamp clear. No sparking wire, electrical arc, explosion or character injury.

PANEL 1 — UPPER LEFT, A HOME IN THE LAMP:
Warm intimate human desk by a softly shadowed room wall. The old brass-and-ivory table lamp is glowing warmly, lighting part of an open book. A tiny creamy flame-headed spirit is visible resting/peering from the sheltered dark seam beneath the base rim, its miniature head and little body fully recognizable. The human-scale base looms above it; the shaft and shade identify this as an ordinary table lamp. The image must immediately say 'a very tiny being lives in the crevice of a human lamp', not 'a child standing next to a small toy lamp'. A partial book and blunt pencil softly establish scale. Cozy amber light, contemplative stillness.

PANEL 2 — UPPER RIGHT, GUIDING EXISTING LIGHT:
Closer view of the SAME lamp and desk. Keep part of the lit lampshade and visible bulb/source within the frame. The tiny spirit braces its short arms against a small TILTED MIRROR/REFLECTIVE GLASS SHARD propped against the lamp base on the tabletop, carefully adjusting its angle. Make the optics narratively legible: a narrow soft warm shaft comes FROM THE EXISTING LAMP above-left, hits the small angled mirror beside the spirit, then changes direction to illuminate the previously dim edge of an open book's page on the right. Two connected legs of the same light path meet AT THE MIRROR, not at the spirit. The book occupies only part of the frame; a gentle bright patch marks the desired destination. Keep the light like illuminated dust and translucent watercolor, not a science-fiction laser. The spirit's hands and chest are NOT shooting beams. Its gesture communicates careful, useful work. Do not draw floating magical light or a new light source. This scene expresses that it helps others by redirecting light.

PANEL 3 — LOWER LEFT, THE HOUSEHOLD HAS MOVED:
A wider, noticeably quieter room view with bare floor, dust outlines where furniture stood, an empty wall hook and a few unlabelled packed cardboard boxes near an open doorway. A much-emptied desk holds the SAME now-unlit old lamp with its unplugged cord hanging loose. The tiny spirit stands at the lamp base on the desk, facing the departing direction. Warm household lighting has disappeared; cool window daylight remains. Show moving through boxes and absence, WITHOUT adding a named family, crying child, pet or distracting human faces. No readable moving labels. This is abandonment through circumstance, not a scary or violent scene. Clearly show the lamp is no longer in use.

PANEL 4 — LOWER MIDDLE, THE BROKEN LAMP / LOST SHELTER:
Low intimate close shot on the bare floor: the SAME lamp has been taken apart and set beside an unlabelled cardboard box. Recognizable round ivory base with its seam now split, brass stem resting at an angle, and the detached ivory glass shade with a single large crack/chipped edge. A couple of small fragments only, not a dangerous field of glass. No lit bulb, no power beam. The tiny wick spirit has climbed out of its old opening and stands just beside the broken base, looking back at the empty shelter with a subdued hesitant posture. The base still dwarfs its body. Reuse the exact lamp design from panels 1 and 2, no replacement oil lamp. Keep the spirit uninjured. Frame lamp and tiny figure clearly inside this narrow slanted panel.

PANEL 5 — LOWER RIGHT, A WANDERER AT DUSK:
A cinematic low, micro-scale view from just outside the empty house's old wooden doorway. The tiny spirit walks LEFT TO RIGHT over the weathered threshold and onto the first damp exterior stone, looking forward into cool gray-blue dusk. Warm light is only the spirit's subtle own glow, which illuminates the immediate tiny area around its feet, not the whole scene. The dark empty interior and the broken lamp are barely visible in the deep background at far left, behind it. A few enormous wind-blown leaves, rough stone seams and heavy cloudy evening sky beyond establish scale and that rain is coming but has not begun. A short edge of old ivy-covered stone wall can lead away to the right, providing a visual handoff to page two where it walks along that wall. DO NOT show the garden gate, greenhouse, mirror puzzle or beast on this origin page. The final spirit is small within the environment, roughly comparable to the reduced tiny figure in Image 1's final panel, NOT an enlarged hero portrait. The emotion is quiet loneliness and setting out to find a place to stay, not triumphant adventure. No backpack, suitcase, staff, cape or umbrella.

CHARACTER IDENTITY:
Exactly the same as Images 2 and 3: creamy ivory oversized flame-shaped head swept backwards, soft blue-gray mottled watercolor shadow patches, simple long black oval eyes, tiny mouth, short little body and round short limbs, small amber flame/leaf-shaped inset in the chest. Very delicate glowing tips and a few ember flecks. No human hair, nose, clothes, animal ears, horns, wings or accessories. One spirit per panel. Thumb-sized relative to all human objects. Flame trails behind when walking right. The visual self-glow is modest and does NOT contradict that its useful ability is redirecting existing external light.

ART DIRECTION:
Same sophisticated watercolor/ink storybook as Image 1: translucent granulated washes, fine irregular ink lines, texture visible, detailed worn wood, ceramic and brass. Warm domestic amber in first two panels transitions into muted gray-green and slate-blue emptiness, finally outdoor dusk. Moody layered shadow silhouettes as in LIMBO, delicate architectural and object illustrations reminiscent of Gorogoa. Never photorealistic, never glossy 3D, no cel-shaded anime faces. No added dialogue or explanatory text. Story readable from images alone.
